anchor.name: Religious Studies
anchor.description: Religious Studies investigates religions—their doctrines, practices, institutions, and social impacts—across cultures and history using humanistic and social-scientific methods. It encompasses theology (doctrine and belief), ritual and worship, scripture and myth, religious experience and mysticism, institutional history (churches, monasteries, hierarchies), and religion's roles in politics, ethic

anchor.name: Cultural Studies
anchor.description: Cultural Studies analyzes how societies create meaning, identity, and power through artifacts, practices, and institutions—popular culture, mass media, consumption, and everyday life. It examines whose interests are served by cultural representations (ideology), how identity is constructed (race, class, gender, nation), and how subordinated groups resist or appropriate dominant meanings. Interdisc

anchor.name: Classics
anchor.description: Classics is the study of ancient Greek and Roman civilizations—their literature (Homer, Sophocles, Virgil), philosophy (Plato, Aristotle), history (Athens, Rome), art and architecture, languages (Ancient Greek, Latin), and their profound influence on Western thought and institutions. Distinguished from History by its focus on textual interpretation and from Philosophy by its historical and cultura

anchor.name: Media Studies
anchor.description: Media Studies investigates how societies create, distribute, and interpret texts through technological systems—newspapers, radio, television, film, the Internet, and social media. It examines media's economic structures (ownership, monopoly, advertising), representational practices (stereotypes, framing, narrative), audience reception and interpretation, and media's roles in politics, culture, and

anchor.name: Gender Studies
anchor.description: Gender Studies examines how gender shapes social institutions, cultural practices, and individual identities across historical and contemporary contexts. It integrates perspectives from history, sociology, anthropology, and literature to analyze gender roles, power relations, and systems of inequality, centering marginalized voices in knowledge production.

anchor.name: Ethnic Studies
anchor.description: Ethnic Studies investigates how ethnicity, race, and cultural identity intersect with power, institutions, and social structures. It examines the histories, cultures, and contemporary experiences of marginalized ethnic and racial groups, analyzing identity formation, discrimination, and resistance while centering the voices and scholarship of communities under study.

anchor.name: Arts & Creative Expression
anchor.description: Creative and performing arts

anchor.name: Visual Arts
anchor.description: Visual Arts encompasses artistic practices that communicate through visual perception—painting, sculpture, photography, and related media. These forms express meaning through color, form, composition, and spatial relationships, distinguishing themselves from performing arts through their static or delayed temporal engagement.

anchor.name: Painting
anchor.description: Painting is the art of creating images by applying pigments to a prepared surface such as canvas or panel. Through brushwork, layering, and color interaction, painters construct visual narratives, explore formal relationships, and express ideas across historical periods and aesthetic movements.

anchor.name: Sculpture
anchor.description: Sculpture is the art of creating three-dimensional works by carving, modeling, casting, or assembling materials such as stone, wood, clay, metal, or found objects. Through volume, surface, and spatial relationships, sculpture engages viewers physically, creating works that occupy, transform, and interact with architectural and landscape environments.

anchor.name: Photography
anchor.description: Photography is the art and practice of creating images by capturing light through a camera's optical system onto a photosensitive surface—film or digital sensor. Photography functions simultaneously as documentation, artistic expression, and visual language, blending technical mastery with aesthetic choice and interpretive vision.

anchor.name: Digital Art
anchor.description: Digital Art encompasses artistic practices that employ digital technologies—computers, software, interactive systems, algorithms—as the primary medium for creation, expression, and presentation. Digital art spans from raster and vector graphics to generative systems and immersive experiences, challenging traditional boundaries between art forms and redefining viewer engagement.

anchor.name: Printmaking
anchor.description: Printmaking is the artistic practice of creating multiple images by transferring pigment from an inked matrix—such as a wood block, engraved plate, stone, or screen—onto paper or another substrate. Printmaking embraces both the technical disciplines of the medium and the conceptual potential of reproducibility, edition, and seriality.

anchor.name: Performing Arts
anchor.description: Performing Arts encompasses artistic disciplines involving live performance before an audience—music, dance, theater, and opera. Distinguished from visual arts by their temporal and embodied nature, performing arts unfold in real time through the performer's physical presence, voice, and interpretive choices, creating ephemeral experiences that exist only in the moment of performance.

anchor.name: Music
anchor.description: Music is the art of organizing sound and silence across time to create meaning, emotion, and aesthetic experience. It functions simultaneously as abstract formal system (melody, harmony, rhythm), cultural expression, social practice, and immediate sensory phenomenon, engaging both intellectual and emotional dimensions of human perception.

anchor.name: Dance
anchor.description: Dance is the kinetic art of coordinated human movement performed to music or rhythm, emphasizing bodily expression and spatial composition.

anchor.name: Theater
anchor.description: Theater is the live dramatic form in which actors perform narrative and emotion through dialogue, movement, and stage design for an immediate audience.

anchor.name: Film
anchor.description: Film is the time-based art of edited moving images projected on a screen, narrating stories through cinematography, montage, and sound design.

anchor.name: Opera
anchor.description: Opera is the dramatic form combining sung vocal performance, orchestral music, narrative, and spectacle into a unified theatrical experience.

anchor.name: Design
anchor.description: Design is the practice of planning and creating visual solutions for communication, products, and environments across graphic, industrial, fashion, interior, and digital domains.

anchor.name: Graphic Design
anchor.description: Graphic design is the creation of visual communication through typography, imagery, and layout applied to printed and digital media.

anchor.name: Industrial Design
anchor.description: Industrial design is the creation of functional and aesthetically coherent three-dimensional products for manufacture and everyday use.

anchor.name: Fashion Design
anchor.description: Fashion design is the creation of garments and accessories for wear, balancing aesthetic expression with functional fit and material behavior.

anchor.name: Interior Design
anchor.description: Interior design is the planning and customization of indoor spaces for function, comfort, and aesthetic coherence through spatial arrangement, materials, and furnishings.

anchor.name: UX/UI Design
anchor.description: UX/UI design is the creation of interactive digital experiences through interface design, user flows, and information architecture.

anchor.name: Crafts
anchor.description: Crafts are handmade objects created through traditional skills and material mastery, emphasizing individual making and the artisan's direct engagement with materials in pottery, textiles, jewelry, glass, and bookbinding.

anchor.name: Pottery & Ceramics
anchor.description: Pottery and ceramics is the craft of shaping clay and mineral bodies through hand-building or wheel-throwing, then hardening through high-temperature firing.

anchor.name: Weaving & Textiles
anchor.description: Weaving and textiles is the craft of interlocking fibers through systematic interlacing on looms or by hand, producing cloth, tapestries, and three-dimensional fabric structures.

anchor.name: Jewelry Making
anchor.description: Jewelry making is the craft of fashioning decorative and wearable objects from metals, gemstones, and found materials using techniques like casting, forging, and stone-setting.

anchor.name: Glassworking
anchor.description: Glassworking is the craft of forming objects from glass through melting, blowing, casting, or cold-working techniques, producing vessels, sculptural forms, and decorative panels.

anchor.name: Bookbinding
anchor.description: Bookbinding is the craft of assembling pages and covers into a durable bound volume through sewing, gluing, and finishing techniques.

anchor.name: Culinary Arts
anchor.description: Culinary arts is the craft and science of preparing, cooking, and presenting food for consumption, encompassing technique, flavor composition, and aesthetic presentation.

anchor.name: Practical Skills & Trades
anchor.description: Hands-on skills and craftsmanship

anchor.name: Construction
anchor.description: Construction is the practice of assembling structural systems, enclosures, and built environments from materials and components through foundations, framing, masonry, roofing, and insulation.

anchor.name: Foundations
anchor.description: Foundations are the structural subsystems that interface between the building and soil, transmitting loads safely into the earth while managing water and settlement through concrete work, excavation, drainage, waterproofing, and load calculations.

anchor.name: Framing
anchor.description: Framing is the assembly of a structural skeleton using beams, columns, joists, and bracing to support the building's weight and resist lateral forces through wood, steel, and composite systems.

anchor.name: Masonry
anchor.description: Masonry is the assembly of individual units—stone, brick, or block—bound with mortar into coherent walls and structures, offering thermal mass, durability, and fire resistance.

anchor.name: Roofing
anchor.description: Roofing comprises the weather-resistant covering layer—shingles, membrane, metal panels, or tiles—that protects the structural frame and interior from precipitation, UV radiation, and thermal extremes.

anchor.name: Insulation
anchor.description: Insulation is the thermal control layer—mineral fiber, foam, or cellulose—installed within walls, roofs, and floors to minimize heat transfer and reduce energy consumption for climate control.

anchor.name: Mechanics
anchor.description: Mechanics is the science and practice of maintaining, repairing, and rebuilding mechanical systems—primarily engines, transmissions, and power-transmission assemblies—to restore function and performance.

anchor.name: Engine Repair
anchor.description: Engine repair encompasses the diagnosis, disassembly, service, and reassembly of internal combustion engines across fuel types and scales, restoring power delivery and fuel efficiency through component reconditioning or replacement.

anchor.name: Transmission Systems
anchor.description: Transmission systems convert engine power into controlled motion at the wheels through gearing ratios, fluid coupling, or electrical transfer. This field covers hydraulic, mechanical, and electronic transmission types used in vehicles, maintenance procedures, and fluid dynamics principles.

anchor.name: Suspension & Steering
anchor.description: Suspension and steering systems maintain vehicle stability and directional control by managing wheel geometry, damping, and driver input translation. This field covers springs, shock absorbers, linkages, and steering mechanisms that isolate the chassis from road impacts while enabling precise handling.

anchor.name: Brake Systems
anchor.description: Brake systems stop or slow vehicles through friction conversion of kinetic energy to heat, using mechanical, hydraulic, or regenerative methods. This field covers drum and disc brake design, fluid mechanics, brake pad composition, anti-lock systems, and service procedures.

anchor.name: Hydraulic Systems
anchor.description: Hydraulic systems transmit and control power using pressurized fluid in sealed circuits, enabling precise force multiplication and remote actuation. This field covers pump operation, pressure regulators, cylinders, motors, and troubleshooting of fluid systems found across vehicles and industrial equipment.

anchor.name: Electronics
anchor.description: Electronics comprises the theory and practice of controlling and conducting electrical current through semiconductor and passive components. This field covers circuit analysis, component behavior, signal processing, and the application of electrical principles to both analog and digital systems.

anchor.name: Basic Circuits
anchor.description: Basic circuits teach foundational electronics through simple combinations of components that demonstrate Ohm's Law, current flow, and energy transfer. This field progresses from component identification and soldering fundamentals through circuit design, measurement techniques, and hands-on troubleshooting methodology.

anchor.name: Microcontrollers
anchor.description: Microcontrollers are compact computing systems on a chip, integrating a processor, memory, and peripherals to enable programmable control of external devices. Microcontrollers execute firmware to read sensors, make decisions, and drive actuators, forming the intelligence in embedded systems.

anchor.name: Power Supplies
anchor.description: Power supplies convert and regulate electrical energy to provide stable, filtered voltage to circuits, transforming wall power into usable direct current at required levels. Power supply design addresses voltage regulation, current capacity, thermal dissipation, and protection against overload.

anchor.name: Radio Electronics
anchor.description: Radio electronics covers wireless transmission and reception of signals, using modulation, antennas, and frequency tuning to send information through air or space. Applications range from AM/FM broadcast receivers to modern Wi-Fi and cellular systems.

anchor.name: Electronics Repair
anchor.description: Electronics repair restores malfunctioning electronic equipment through component diagnosis, part replacement, and circuit rework. Repair technicians use oscilloscopes and multimeters to locate faults, desolder and solder components, and verify function before returning equipment to service.

anchor.name: Plumbing
anchor.description: Plumbing encompasses the design, installation, and maintenance of systems for water supply, drainage, and gas distribution in buildings. This field covers pipe materials, fittings, regulations, and repair techniques essential for delivering clean water and safely removing waste.

anchor.name: Pipe Systems
anchor.description: Pipe systems distribute water and gas through buildings using metal, plastic, or composite materials selected for pressure rating, corrosion resistance, and cost. Pipe sizing, layout, and joinery techniques ensure proper flow and prevent leaks in both supply and drainage applications.

anchor.name: Fixtures Installation
anchor.description: Fixtures installation positions and secures sinks, toilets, showers, faucets, and other water-using appliances within buildings, connecting them to supply and drainage networks. Proper installation ensures watertight seals, correct operation, and access for future maintenance.

anchor.name: Water Heating
anchor.description: Water heating systems generate hot water for domestic and commercial use through electric resistance, gas combustion, or renewable energy methods. System selection considers capacity, efficiency, space constraints, and local fuel availability.

anchor.name: Drainage Systems
anchor.description: Drainage systems remove used water and waste from buildings through sloped pipe networks that flow to municipal sewers or septic systems. Proper pitch, venting, and trap design prevent blockages, backflow, and odor problems.

anchor.name: Plumbing Repair
anchor.description: Plumbing repair addresses leaks, clogs, frozen pipes, and failed fixtures by locating problems through inspection and pressure testing, then replacing components or clearing blockages. Emergency repairs stabilize damage; permanent repairs restore full function.

anchor.name: Carpentry
anchor.description: Carpentry is the craft of designing, building, and finishing wooden structures and furnishings through hand and power tools. This field encompasses structural framing, finish carpentry, joinery methods, and wood selection for aesthetics and durability.

anchor.name: Joinery
anchor.description: Joinery is the art of connecting wooden pieces using mechanical joints—mortise-and-tenon, dovetails, box joints, and dowels—rather than nails or screws. Strong, durable joinery creates furniture and structures that endure without fastener corrosion or creep.

anchor.name: Furniture Making
anchor.description: Furniture making designs and builds functional decorative pieces—tables, chairs, cabinets, and beds—using wood selection, finishing, and assembly to blend form with utility. Each piece balances aesthetics, structural integrity, and material economy.

anchor.name: Cabinetry
anchor.description: Cabinetry is the specialized craft of building custom fitted wooden storage and display cabinets integrated into architectural spaces. Precision joinery, wood movement accommodation, and hardware selection are critical for seamless function and appearance.

anchor.name: Wood Finishing
anchor.description: Wood finishing applies protective and aesthetic coatings—stains, oils, waxes, and varnishes—to enhance color, texture, and durability. Proper surface preparation, application technique, and curing ensure finishes protect against moisture, scratches, and environmental damage.

anchor.name: Wood Restoration
anchor.description: Wood restoration returns damaged, aged, or worn wooden pieces to functional and aesthetic condition through assessment, cleaning, repair, and refinishing. Restoration preserves original character while addressing structural issues and surface deterioration.

anchor.name: Welding
anchor.description: Welding joins metal pieces by melting and fusing them together with heat, creating permanent structural bonds. This field encompasses arc, gas, and resistance welding methods, safety protocols, metallurgy principles, and inspection techniques.

anchor.name: Arc Welding
anchor.description: Arc welding creates a localized electrical arc between an electrode and workpiece that heats metal to melting and fuses it. Shielded Metal Arc Welding (SMAW), Gas Metal Arc Welding (GMAW), and Flux-Cored Arc Welding (FCAW) are common arc methods suited for thick material and field work.

anchor.name: MIG Welding
anchor.description: MIG welding uses a semiautomatic process where a continuously fed wire electrode and shielding gas create an arc. MIG is fast, clean, and beginner-friendly, making it ideal for thin sheet metal and production work.

anchor.name: TIG Welding
anchor.description: TIG welding uses a non-consumable tungsten electrode and inert gas shielding to produce high-quality welds with precise control, excelling on thin materials and stainless steel. Distinct from arc and MIG welding by its manual electrode positioning and from gas welding by its electrical power source.

anchor.name: Gas Welding
anchor.description: Gas welding melts metal using an open flame from burning acetylene or other gases, typically oxy-acetylene, producing lower temperatures and simpler equipment than electrical methods. Predates electrical welding and remains valuable for portable fieldwork and certain repairs.

anchor.name: Welding Safety
anchor.description: Welding safety encompasses hazard prevention and protective protocols for all welding methods, including arc-radiation protection for eyes and skin, respiratory safety from fumes, and fire prevention. Applies across every welding process, managing risk rather than technique.

anchor.name: Gardening
anchor.description: Gardening cultivates and maintains plants for food, ornament, or ecological purposes, encompassing soil management, planting, growth maintenance, and pest management. Bridges practical horticulture through multiple interdependent subdisciplines rather than a single isolated skill.

anchor.name: Soil Preparation
anchor.description: Soil preparation readies growing beds and field plots for planting by tilling, amending with compost or nutrients, and testing pH and structure. Establishes the foundation for plant establishment, preceding and distinct from planting, maintenance pruning, and pest control.

anchor.name: Planting Techniques
anchor.description: Planting techniques select appropriate depth, spacing, timing, and methods for seeds or seedlings to ensure healthy establishment and vigor. Distinct from preceding soil preparation and from maintenance pruning and pest control.

anchor.name: Pruning
anchor.description: Pruning removes dead, diseased, or overgrown plant parts to promote healthy structure, shape, and productivity through clean cuts that heal effectively. Maintains established plants during active growth, distinct from initial planting and from pest intervention.

anchor.name: Pest Control
anchor.description: Pest control prevents or eliminates insects, mites, fungi, and other organisms that damage crops or ornamental plants through biological, chemical, or mechanical methods. Addresses external threats to established plants, distinct from soil preparation, planting, and pruning.

anchor.name: Composting
anchor.description: Composting decomposes organic waste—leaves, kitchen scraps, manure—into nutrient-rich humus that improves soil fertility and structure for future planting. Produces an amendment input for soil preparation, closing the cycle between waste and bed improvement.

anchor.name: Cooking
anchor.description: Cooking transforms raw ingredients into prepared food through heat and technique, encompassing method mastery, flavor development, and food safety. A practical art spanning multiple specialized domains rather than a single unified skill.

anchor.name: Basic Techniques
anchor.description: Basic cooking techniques—sautéing, boiling, roasting, braising, grilling, simmering—form the foundation for all savory preparation and distinguish everyday cuisine from baking, preservation, and specialized dietary approaches.

anchor.name: Baking
anchor.description: Baking uses controlled heat in an oven to cook breads, cakes, pastries, and other items where chemistry and precise timing create structure and texture. Requires exact measurements and regulated conditions, fundamentally different from stovetop and grill methods.

anchor.name: Food Preservation
anchor.description: Food preservation extends shelf life through canning, freezing, drying, salting, fermenting, or curing, preventing spoilage and enabling storage across seasons. Transforms fresh food into shelf-stable products rather than cooking for immediate consumption.

anchor.name: Nutrition
anchor.description: Nutrition science examines how foods and their components affect body function, health, and disease prevention, informing ingredient selection and meal composition. Provides the biological rationale behind cooking choices, distinct from technique execution and special-diet implementation.

anchor.name: Special Diets
anchor.description: Special diets accommodate allergies, intolerances, ethical commitments, medical conditions, or cultural preferences by modifying ingredients and preparation methods. Applies cooking techniques and nutritional knowledge to specific dietary goals or constraints.

anchor.name: Sewing
anchor.description: Sewing joins fabric using needle and thread to create or repair garments and textiles, combining pattern interpretation, hand control, and material understanding. A standalone practical craft independent from mechanics, construction, and other trades.

anchor.name: Automotive
anchor.description: Automotive encompasses operation, maintenance, and repair of motor vehicles, blending mechanical, electrical, and diagnostic knowledge to keep engines, drivetrains, and systems functioning. A broad applied discipline distinct from pure mechanics by its vehicle-specific focus.

anchor.name: Survival & Emergency Preparedness
anchor.description: Critical knowledge for emergencies

anchor.name: First Aid & Medical
anchor.description: First aid and medical knowledge provides immediate emergency care and stabilization for injuries and illness when professional medical help is absent, encompassing assessment, intervention, and triage. Spans immediate treatment through sustained care in resource-constrained settings.

anchor.name: Basic First Aid
anchor.description: Basic first aid addresses common injuries and medical emergencies—choking, unconsciousness, wounds, burns, fractures, shock—using standard assessment and response protocols to stabilize and prepare for transport. Provides foundational life-saving techniques distinct from trauma surgery or wilderness-specific interventions.

anchor.name: Trauma Care
anchor.description: Trauma care manages severe, life-threatening injuries requiring advanced techniques: hemorrhage control beyond basic pressure, chest decompression for pneumothorax, spinal stabilization, and airway management in austere conditions. Escalates beyond basic first aid by addressing penetrating and crush injuries in resource-scarce settings.

anchor.name: Wilderness Medicine
anchor.description: Wilderness medicine adapts first aid and trauma care to remote or resource-scarce environments where professional evacuation is delayed or impossible, incorporating environmental hazards (hypothermia, altitude sickness, dehydration, venomous bites) and improvised materials. Extends standard protocols by addressing extended self-care, evacuation delays, and environmental stressors.

anchor.name: Emergency Childbirth
anchor.description: Emergency childbirth manages imminent or in-progress labor outside a medical facility, covering labor-progression assessment, delivery assistance, placenta delivery, and immediate postpartum care for mother and infant. Handles a normal physiological process accelerated by circumstance, distinct from trauma, infection, or pathological illness.

anchor.name: Medication Knowledge
anchor.description: Medication knowledge encompasses pharmacological understanding—drug categories, mechanisms of action, side effects, interactions, and proper administration—applied to emergency and survival contexts. Provides informed decision-making for treatment, balancing benefit against risk when professional pharmacological guidance is absent.

anchor.name: Water Procurement & Purification
anchor.description: Water procurement and purification comprises the location, extraction, and treatment of water sources to ensure potability and safety, foundational to survival as the human body cannot function without regular hydration.

anchor.name: Finding Water Sources
anchor.description: Finding water sources involves locating natural and artificial supplies of fresh water through observation of landscape features, biological indicators, and precipitation collection, distinguishing viable sources from contaminated or inaccessible ones.

anchor.name: Purification Methods
anchor.description: Purification methods remove or neutralize biological, chemical, and physical contaminants from water through distinct processes including thermal, chemical, and mechanical approaches, ensuring safety for consumption and medical use.

anchor.name: Water Storage
anchor.description: Water storage preserves potable water in sealed containers for extended periods using protection against light, contamination, and biological growth, essential for bridging supply gaps during procurement disruptions or dry seasons.

anchor.name: Water Testing
anchor.description: Water testing assesses potability through visual, sensory, and chemical examination to detect microbial contamination, mineral content, and chemical hazards, enabling informed treatment decisions and confirmation of purification success.

anchor.name: Water Conservation
anchor.description: Water conservation minimizes consumption through rationing, leak prevention, and reuse of water for multiple purposes, extending supply availability during shortages and reducing the labor required for procurement and purification.

anchor.name: Food Preservation & Storage
anchor.description: Food preservation and storage extends the shelf life of perishable foodstuffs through various chemical, thermal, and microbiological techniques, enabling long-term food security independent of seasonal availability and supply chains.

anchor.name: Canning & Jarring
anchor.description: Canning and jarring seals cooked food in glass containers with heat-processed seals to exclude oxygen and pathogens, enabling shelf-stable storage for years and distinguishing this thermal-based method from other preservation approaches.

anchor.name: Drying & Dehydration
anchor.description: Drying and dehydration removes water from food through exposure to heat and air circulation, halting microbial growth and enzymatic spoilage while concentrating nutrients and flavors, one of humanity's oldest preservation methods.

anchor.name: Smoking Meats
anchor.description: Smoking meats applies wood smoke to preserve meat through simultaneous cooking, drying, and antimicrobial coating, imparting flavor and extending storage life while distinguishing this method from other heat-based food preservation.

anchor.name: Salting & Curing
anchor.description: Salting and curing preserves meat and fish by drawing out moisture through osmosis using salt, creating a hostile environment for pathogens and enabling storage without refrigeration, historically the dominant preservation method across cultures.

anchor.name: Fermentation
anchor.description: Fermentation preserves vegetables and other foods through controlled microbial action that produces lactic acid, creating acidity that inhibits spoilage organisms while developing complex flavors and increasing nutrient bioavailability.

anchor.name: Shelter Construction
anchor.description: Shelter construction creates protective structures using available materials and techniques suited to climate and terrain, providing insulation from elements, security from predators, and psychological safety essential for extended survival.

anchor.name: Temporary Shelters
anchor.description: Temporary shelters provide rapid protection using lightweight materials and simple construction requiring minimal tools, suitable for emergency situations, transit camps, or short-term occupation before permanent establishment.

anchor.name: Permanent Structures
anchor.description: Permanent structures provide long-term shelter using durable materials and techniques designed for year-round habitation, incorporating weatherproofing, structural stability, and features supporting daily life and safety.

anchor.name: Insulation Techniques
anchor.description: Insulation techniques reduce heat transfer between interior and exterior through barriers of trapped air, reflective surfaces, or thermal mass, critical for maintaining comfortable temperature without excessive fuel consumption.

anchor.name: Underground Shelters
anchor.description: Underground shelters utilize earth structures for thermal stability and protection from surface hazards, offering natural insulation and radiation shielding while presenting challenges in ventilation, moisture control, and construction difficulty.

anchor.name: Building Materials
anchor.description: Building materials encompass substances used in shelter construction including wood, stone, earth, metal, and plant fibers, selected for availability, durability, thermal properties, and suitability to local climate conditions.

anchor.name: Fire Making
anchor.description: Fire making produces combustion through ignition of fuel using friction, sparks, or chemical reactions, essential for warmth, cooking, water purification, psychological comfort, and tool hardening across survival contexts.

anchor.name: Friction Methods
anchor.description: Friction methods generate heat and ignition through mechanical rubbing of wood against wood, using bow drills or hand drills to concentrate pressure and velocity until spontaneous combustion occurs.

anchor.name: Spark Methods
anchor.description: Spark methods strike ferrous materials such as flint against steel or use chemical reactions to produce ignition-capable sparks, requiring tinder that catches and sustains the flame until kindling accepts full combustion.

anchor.name: Fire Maintenance
anchor.description: Fire maintenance sustains and controls established flames through fuel management, airflow regulation, and heat distribution, distinguishing the active tending of fire from its initial creation.

anchor.name: Fuel Types
anchor.description: Fuel types encompass materials burned to sustain fire including dry wood, charcoal, plant matter, animal fats, and mineral oils, selected for combustibility, heat output, smoke characteristics, and local availability.

anchor.name: Fire Safety
anchor.description: Fire safety encompasses hazard prevention and damage control around established flames, including water reserves, firebreak creation, and smoke management to prevent uncontrolled spread and injury.

anchor.name: Navigation
anchor.description: Navigation determines location and direction of travel through observation of natural features, celestial bodies, magnetic instruments, and maps, enabling purposeful movement across unfamiliar terrain without electronic aids.

anchor.name: Celestial Navigation
anchor.description: Celestial navigation uses the positions of stars, planets, and the sun to determine geographic coordinates and heading, providing direction and latitude-longitude reference points independent of magnetic fields or ground features.

anchor.name: Compass Usage
anchor.description: Compass usage applies magnetic-needle orientation instruments to determine cardinal directions and maintain bearing across terrain, assuming magnetic declination awareness and functioning equipment to prevent navigation errors.

anchor.name: Natural Navigation
anchor.description: Natural navigation uses environmental cues—stars, sun position, terrain features, wind patterns—to determine location and direction without instruments. It combines celestial observation with landscape reading, enabling wayfinding when technology fails.

anchor.name: Map Reading
anchor.description: Map reading is the interpretation of cartographic symbols, scale, and spatial relationships to determine current position and plan routes. It converts two-dimensional representations into three-dimensional environmental understanding.

anchor.name: GPS Alternatives
anchor.description: GPS alternatives are non-electronic positioning techniques including dead reckoning, terrain association, and celestial observation. These methods provide location determination when satellite systems are unavailable or unreliable.

anchor.name: Emergency Communication
anchor.description: Emergency communication encompasses technologies and protocols for establishing contact during crises when normal infrastructure is damaged or overwhelmed. It spans radio systems, visual codes, and decentralized networks enabling coordinated response.

anchor.name: Radio Communication
anchor.description: Radio communication uses electromagnetic waves to transmit voice or data across distance. In emergency contexts, it provides reliable long-range contact independent of wired infrastructure.

anchor.name: Visual Signaling
anchor.description: Visual signaling communicates through light, color, or gesture—mirrors reflecting sunlight, smoke signals, flag codes, or hand gestures. It requires no electronic equipment and works across line of sight.

anchor.name: Morse Code
anchor.description: Morse code encodes messages as sequences of dots and dashes transmitted via sound, light, or radio. It enabled long-distance communication before voice transmission and remains useful in low-bandwidth emergency scenarios.

anchor.name: Emergency Codes
anchor.description: Emergency codes are standardized signal sequences—SOS, MAYDAY, PAN, securite—recognized internationally by rescue and maritime authorities. They compress urgent information into brief, unmistakable patterns.

anchor.name: Mesh Networks
anchor.description: Mesh networks distribute communication across multiple nodes where each device relays messages for others, eliminating dependence on central infrastructure. They function even when individual nodes fail or go offline.

anchor.name: Defense & Security
anchor.description: Defense and security encompasses strategies and techniques for protecting persons and resources from threats including violence, theft, and coercion. It ranges from awareness and avoidance to direct resistance methods.

anchor.name: Disaster Response
anchor.description: Disaster response encompasses organized procedures for mitigating impacts of large-scale catastrophic events—earthquakes, floods, hurricanes—through coordinated deployment of resources, evacuation, and recovery operations.

anchor.name: Psychological Resilience
anchor.description: Psychological resilience is the mental and emotional capacity to maintain function and purpose despite prolonged stress, loss, or trauma. It develops through preparation, community connection, and practiced coping strategies.

anchor.name: Reference & Documentation
anchor.description: Essential reference materials

anchor.name: Encyclopedias
anchor.description: Encyclopedias are comprehensive general-knowledge reference works organizing information alphabetically or by subject. They synthesize established knowledge from multiple domains into accessible, cross-referenced entries.

anchor.name: Dictionaries
anchor.description: Dictionaries are repositories mapping words to definitions, etymologies, and usage examples within a language. They preserve semantic precision and document how meaning shifts across historical periods.

anchor.name: Technical Manuals
anchor.description: Technical manuals are instructional documents detailing operation, maintenance, repair, or assembly of equipment and systems. They translate design intent into step-by-step guidance for users and technicians.

anchor.name: Maps & Atlases
anchor.description: Maps and atlases are spatial representations showing geography, political boundaries, infrastructure networks, or thematic data distribution. They encode complex geographic relationships into visual form.

anchor.name: Standards & Specifications
anchor.description: Standards and specifications are formalized technical requirements and measurement baselines for materials, components, and processes. They enable interoperability and consistent quality across manufacturers and contexts.

anchor.name: Formulas & Tables
anchor.description: Formulas and tables are mathematical expressions and data compilations enabling calculation and reference lookup. They compress knowledge into compact, reusable forms for engineering, science, and commerce.

anchor.name: Protocols & Procedures
anchor.description: Protocols and procedures are documented sequences of steps for conducting operations, experiments, diplomatic exchanges, or medical treatments. They standardize methods and ensure reproducibility across practitioners and contexts.

anchor.name: Blueprints & Schematics
anchor.description: Blueprints and schematics are technical drawings showing construction, electrical, mechanical, or architectural design details. They translate design concepts into precise specifications for fabrication and assembly.

anchor.name: Patents
anchor.description: Patents are legal documents recording inventions, their novel technical features, functional principles, and enforceable claims. They balance knowledge disclosure against temporary monopoly rights for inventors.

anchor.name: Historical Archives
anchor.description: Historical archives are primary-source collections preserving records of past events, institutions, and persons—letters, photographs, government documents, business ledgers. They provide evidence for understanding history beyond published accounts.

anchor.name: Cultural Preservation
anchor.description: Human culture and heritage

anchor.name: Languages
anchor.description: Languages are systematic sets of symbols and rules enabling communication within and between communities. They encode cultural concepts, historical experience, and unique perspectives on meaning.

anchor.name: Language Dictionaries
anchor.description: Language dictionaries document vocabulary and definitions specific to individual languages. They preserve lexical precision and show how meaning develops within a linguistic system.

anchor.name: Grammars
anchor.description: Grammars are formal descriptions of linguistic structure—phonology, morphology, syntax—and conjugation rules governing word formation and sentence construction. They make implicit language patterns explicit for learning and analysis.

anchor.name: Endangered Languages
anchor.description: Endangered languages are languages with few remaining speakers facing extinction without active preservation efforts. They represent unique worldviews and cultural knowledge at risk of permanent loss.

anchor.name: Sign Languages
anchor.description: Sign languages are complete human languages expressed through manual gestures, hand positions, and facial expressions. They enable full linguistic and cultural participation for deaf and hard-of-hearing communities.

anchor.name: Translation Resources
anchor.description: Translation resources are tools and references—glossaries, terminology databases, parallel texts—enabling conversion of meaning between language pairs. They bridge linguistic distance while acknowledging irreducible cultural differences.

anchor.name: Folklore & Mythology
anchor.description: Folklore and mythology are narrative and belief systems explaining cultural origins, moral values, and natural phenomena through story. They preserve pre-literate knowledge and encode community identity.

anchor.name: Traditions & Customs
anchor.description: Traditions and customs are established social practices—greetings, celebrations, dress codes—passed through generations within communities. They embody cultural values and reinforce social cohesion.

anchor.name: Traditional Recipes
anchor.description: Traditional recipes are documented food-preparation methods embodying regional and cultural identity. They preserve culinary knowledge and connect communities to land, ingredients, and history.

anchor.name: Music & Songs
anchor.description: Music and songs are vocal and instrumental compositions integral to cultural expression, ritual, and social bonding. They transmit emotional and spiritual meaning across generations through performance.

anchor.name: Stories & Narratives
anchor.description: Stories and narratives are fictional and historical accounts preserving cultural experience, wisdom, and values. They transmit lessons and meaning through plot, character, and metaphor across time.

anchor.name: Games & Recreation
anchor.description: Games and recreation are competitive or leisure activities reflecting cultural values and social structures. They encode learning, skill development, and community participation in structured play.

anchor.name: Rituals & Ceremonies
anchor.description: Rituals and ceremonies are formalized practices marking significant cultural, spiritual, or lifecycle moments—birth, coming of age, marriage, death. They externalize internal transitions and reinforce community identity.

anchor.name: Traditional Art Techniques
anchor.description: Traditional art techniques are craft methods and aesthetic practices maintained across generations—weaving, metalwork, carving, painting. They preserve manual skill and aesthetic sensibility specific to cultural contexts.

anchor.name: Oral Histories
anchor.description: Oral histories are spoken accounts of past events and family lineages transmitted across generations without written documentation. They preserve personal experience and community memory outside institutional archives.

anchor.name: Digital Preservation
anchor.description: Digital formats and preservation

anchor.name: File Formats
anchor.description: File formats are standardized encoding schemes defining how data is stored and interpreted digitally. They enable software interoperability and long-term digital preservation across platform and time.

anchor.name: Document Formats
anchor.description: Document formats are file structures for encoding text, layout, metadata, and formatting—PDF, DOCX, ODT. They preserve content and visual presentation across software versions and operating systems.

anchor.name: Image Formats
anchor.description: Image formats are encoding standards for visual data including raster formats storing pixel grids—JPEG, PNG—and vector formats encoding geometric shapes and paths—SVG, EPS. Each format balances compression, quality, and scalability differently.

anchor.name: Audio Formats
anchor.description: Standardized codecs and container specifications for encoding and storing acoustic information—ranging from lossy compression formats (MP3, AAC) to lossless preservation (FLAC, WAV). Distinct from visual media by encoding temporal sound waves rather than visual intensity or motion data.

anchor.name: Video Formats
anchor.description: Standardized codecs and container specifications for encoding and storing visual frame sequences—ranging from lossy streaming formats (H.264, VP9) to lossless capture (ProRes, DNxHD). Distinct from audio by encoding spatial intensity and motion rather than temporal frequency content, and from still images by the intrinsic time dimension.

anchor.name: Archive Formats
anchor.description: Standardized container and compression methods for bundling and reducing digital file sizes—including both compression-focused formats (ZIP, 7z, RAR) and streaming archives (TAR). Distinct from media codecs by operating at the file-aggregation level rather than stream encoding, enabling efficient transport and storage of multi-file collections.

anchor.name: Compression Methods
anchor.description: Techniques and algorithms for reducing data volume through mathematical transformation—balancing information density against decompression overhead. Includes lossless methods (Huffman, DEFLATE) that preserve fidelity and lossy methods (transform coding, quantization) that tolerate reconstruction error; orthogonal to encryption which protects confidentiality rather than reducing size.

anchor.name: Encryption & Security
anchor.description: Cryptographic protection of data confidentiality and integrity during storage and transmission—spanning symmetric ciphers (AES, ChaCha20) for shared-key encryption and asymmetric methods (RSA, ECDSA) for key exchange and authentication. Distinct from compression by prioritizing secrecy and tamper-detection over size reduction.

anchor.name: Backup Strategies
anchor.description: Systematic replication of data across geographically or logically distinct storage media—including full copies (mirror), incremental snapshots, and versioned archives. Ensures recovery from hardware failure, data corruption, and accidental deletion; complements but is distinct from archival formats and compression which address density and longevity separately.

anchor.name: Data Recovery
anchor.description: Techniques for reconstructing or accessing lost or inaccessible data—including disk imaging, partition repair, logical file recovery from overwritten storage, and data forensics. Presupposes backup and storage redundancy failures; distinct from backup strategies by operating post-disaster when primary data is already unavailable.

anchor.name: Post-Disaster Rebuilding
anchor.description: Knowledge for rebuilding civilization

anchor.name: Basic Infrastructure
anchor.description: Essential physical systems and technologies required to restore basic societal function after large-scale infrastructure failure—including energy generation, water access, waste containment, information exchange, and local transport. Serves as the load-bearing foundation upon which tool-making, medicine, and community decision-making can rebuild.

anchor.name: Basic Power Generation
anchor.description: Methods and devices for converting natural energy sources into usable electrical power—including human-powered systems (hand cranks, pedals), gravitational fall (water wheels), and combustion of stored fuel. Foundational to all technical recovery; enables water pumping, communication, food preservation, and manufacturing.

anchor.name: Water Systems
anchor.description: Technologies for accessing, purifying, and distributing fresh water—including gravity-fed collection, mechanical or chemical filtration, and preventing microbial contamination. Distinct from sanitation by addressing source and potability rather than waste disposal; essential for drinking, cooking, agriculture, and disease prevention.

anchor.name: Sanitation
anchor.description: Methods for containing and processing human and organic waste to prevent disease transmission and environmental contamination—including composting, latrine construction, and grey-water separation. Distinct from water systems by addressing excreta and runoff rather than drinking-water sourcing; foundational to public health in dense settlements.

anchor.name: Communication Networks
anchor.description: Infrastructure and methods for transmitting information over distance—including messenger systems, signal relay (smoke, light, sound), and wireless/electrical networks. Enables coordination between settlements, warning dissemination, and knowledge sharing; distinct from transportation by moving information rather than physical goods or people.

anchor.name: Basic Transportation
anchor.description: Technologies and infrastructure for moving people and goods across local distances—including animal traction, wheeled vehicles, watercraft, and footpaths. Supports trade, resource distribution, and emergency mobility; distinct from communication systems by transporting material cargo rather than information.

anchor.name: Tool Making
anchor.description: Fabrication and refinement of implements and mechanical systems—including metallurgy, woodworking, and assembly of hand tools. Presupposes basic energy availability and raw materials; supports agriculture, construction, and specialized crafts; distinct from chemistry by focusing on mechanical form rather than molecular transformation.

anchor.name: Essential Chemistry
anchor.description: Fundamental chemical processes and reactions applicable to survival—including soap-making, fermentation, water disinfection, and soil amendment. Operates at the scale of household and field rather than industrial synthesis; enables food preservation, hygiene, and agricultural productivity distinct from medicine which focuses on disease treatment.

anchor.name: Basic Medicine Production
anchor.description: Production and application of remedies for disease and injury using available plants and minerals—including herbalism, wound management, and fermentation-based preservation. Operates on empirical knowledge and traditional formulations rather than industrial pharmaceuticals; distinct from general chemistry by targeting health intervention and restoration.

anchor.name: Community Organization
anchor.description: Frameworks and practices for collective decision-making, resource allocation, and conflict resolution—including governance structures, work coordination, and knowledge sharing protocols. Integrates outcomes from infrastructure, tool-making, and medicine into coherent social systems; distinct from technical domains by operating on human coordination rather than material transformation.

physics_01_01.name: Kinematics

physics_01_01.name: Motion equations

physics_01_01.name: Projectile motion
physics_01_01.description: Two-dimensional motion of a body launched into a gravitational field, combining uniform horizontal velocity with uniformly accelerated vertical fall. Covers trajectory shape, range, time of flight and maximum height, typically neglecting or explicitly modelling air resistance.

physics_01_01.name: Circular motion
physics_01_01.description: Motion along a circular path: angular velocity, period and frequency, and the centripetal acceleration directed toward the centre that keeps the body on the curve. Includes uniform and non-uniform cases and the relations between angular and linear quantities.

physics_01_01.name: Relative motion

physics_01_01.name: Reference frames

Complements Relative motion, which handles the velocity arithmetic between frames.

physics_01_01.name: Dynamics

physics_01_01.name: Newton's laws

physics_01_01.name: Forces and interactions

physics_01_01.name: Work and energy
physics_01_01.description: Work done by forces, kinetic and potential energy, power, the work–energy theorem and conservation of mechanical energy — scalar tools for solving motion problems without tracking forces through time.

physics_01_01.name: Momentum

physics_01_01.name: Collisions

physics_01_01.name: Statics

physics_01_01.name: Fluid Mechanics

physics_01_01.name: Oscillations & Waves

Electromagnetic waves belong under Electromagnetism.

physics_01_01.name: Quantum Foundations

physics_01_01.name: Quantum Field Theory
